name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q01 - Chemicals released at the synaptic junction

questiontext.text: Chemicals which are released at the synaptic junction are called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
At a chemical synapse, the membranes of the pre-synaptic and post-synaptic neurons are separated by a fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft. Impulse transmission across this gap requires specific chemical messengers.

Step 2: Evaluation
When an action potential reaches the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of synaptic vesicles toward the pre-synaptic membrane, where they fuse and release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. In contrast, hormones are secreted by endocrine glands into the bloodstream, cerebrospinal fluid cushions the brain and spinal cord, and lymph is part of the lymphatic and immune system.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The chemicals released at the synaptic junction are called neurotransmitters.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q02 - Ions responsible for resting membrane potential

questiontext.text: Potential difference across resting membrane is negative. This is due to differential distribution of the following ions

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A resting neuron maintains a polarised state across its axonal membrane, where the inner surface is negatively charged relative to the outer surface. This electrical potential difference is called the resting membrane potential.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the resting state, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to potassium ions (\(\mathrm{K}^{+}\)) and nearly impermeable to sodium ions (\(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\)), as well as impermeable to negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm. Consequently, the axoplasm contains a high concentration of \(\mathrm{K}^{+}\) and negatively charged proteins with low \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\), whereas the extracellular fluid has a high concentration of \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\) and low \(\mathrm{K}^{+}\). Ions such as \(\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{++}\), \(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\), \(\mathrm{Ca}^{++}\), and \(\mathrm{Mg}^{++}\) do not establish this primary resting ionic gradient across the axonal membrane.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The negative potential difference across the resting membrane is due to the differential distribution of \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\) and \(\mathrm{K}^{+}\) ions.

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To preserve the polarised state of a resting neuron, the concentration gradients of sodium and potassium ions across the axonal membrane must be actively maintained against passive diffusion.

Step 2: Evaluation
The ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the active transport of ions through the sodium-potassium ion pump, which transports \(3\,\mathrm{Na}^{+}\) outwards for \(2\,\mathrm{K}^{+}\) into the cell using ATP. Hormones regulate systemic physiological processes and neurotransmitters mediate synaptic transmission, rather than maintaining the resting axonal membrane potential.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Resting membrane potential is maintained by an ion pump.

questiontext.text: The function of our visceral organs is controlled by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The peripheral neural system is divided into the somatic neural system, which relays impulses from the central nervous system to skeletal muscles (voluntary control), and the autonomic neural system, which transmits impulses from the central nervous system to involuntary organs and smooth muscles.

Step 2: Evaluation
The autonomic neural system is further classified into the sympathetic neural system and the parasympathetic neural system. Together, these two divisions regulate the involuntary activities of visceral organs such as the heart, lungs, and digestive tract. The somatic neural system controls voluntary skeletal muscles rather than visceral organs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The function of visceral organs is controlled by the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural system.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q05 - Components not involved in knee-jerk reflex

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not involved in Knee-jerk reflex?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A reflex action is an involuntary response to a peripheral nervous stimulation that occurs without conscious effort or thought, mediated through a reflex arc at the level of the spinal cord.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the knee-jerk reflex, tapping the patellar tendon stretches the muscle spindle (receptor), which generates an impulse carried by an afferent neuron through the dorsal root ganglion into the spinal cord. Within the spinal cord, the impulse is transmitted to an efferent (motor) neuron (with interneurons shown in the spinal cord reflex pathway diagram for reciprocal inhibition), which stimulates the effector muscle to contract. The brain is not directly involved in executing this spinal reflex arc.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The brain is not involved in the knee-jerk reflex.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q06 - Brain area associated with strong emotions

questiontext.text: An area in the brain which is associated with strong emotions is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different regions of the human brain are specialized for distinct sensory, motor, homeostatic, and emotional functions.

Step 2: Evaluation
The inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres and a group of associated deep structures such as the amygdala and hippocampus form a complex structure called the limbic lobe or limbic system. Along with the hypothalamus, the limbic system is involved in the regulation of sexual behaviour and the expression of emotional reactions such as excitement, pleasure, rage, and fear. By contrast, the cerebral cortex mediates complex sensory, motor, and association functions, the cerebellum coordinates posture and balance, and the medulla controls vital autonomic functions like respiration and cardiovascular reflexes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The area in the brain associated with strong emotions is the limbic system.

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photoreceptor cells in the retina (rods and cones) contain light-sensitive proteins called photopigments that are composed of opsin (a protein) and retinal (a light-absorbing chromophore).

Step 2: Evaluation
Rod cells contain a purplish-red protein called rhodopsin (visual purple), which contains retinal, an aldehyde derivative of Vitamin A. Light induces dissociation of retinal from opsin, leading to changes in membrane permeability and generation of action potentials. Vitamins B, C, and D do not form the chromophore of rhodopsin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The vitamin present in rhodopsin is Vitamin A (Vit A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q08 - Structures enclosed by the human eyeball

questiontext.text: Human eyeball consists of three layers and it encloses

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The wall of the human eyeball is composed of three concentric layers: the external sclera (with the anterior cornea), the middle choroid (which forms the ciliary body and iris), and the inner retina.

Step 2: Evaluation
Inside these three layers, the eyeball encloses a transparent crystalline lens held in place by ligaments attached to the ciliary body. The space between the cornea and the lens (the aqueous chamber) contains a thin watery fluid called aqueous humor, while the space between the lens and the retina (the vitreous chamber) is filled with a transparent gel called vitreous humor. The cornea and iris are parts of the eyeball wall layers themselves, and the optic nerve exits posteriorly rather than being enclosed within the chambers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The human eyeball consists of three layers and encloses the lens, aqueous humor, and vitreous humor.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q09 - Wax secreting gland in ear canal

questiontext.text: Wax secreting gland present in the ear canal is called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The external auditory meatus (ear canal) leads inwards from the pinna to the tympanic membrane and contains fine hairs and specialized wax-secreting glands for protection.

Step 2: Evaluation
The wax-secreting glands in the skin of the external auditory meatus are modified sweat glands known as ceruminous glands, which produce earwax (cerumen) to trap dust and microbes. Sweat glands secrete watery sweat for thermoregulation, while prostate glands and Cowper's (bulbourethral) glands are male reproductive accessory glands.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The wax-secreting gland present in the ear canal is called the ceruminous gland.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q10 - Part of internal ear for hearing

questiontext.text: The part of internal ear responsible for hearing is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The internal ear (labyrinth) performs two major sensory functions: hearing and maintenance of body balance and posture.

Step 2: Evaluation
The coiled portion of the labyrinth is called the cochlea, which houses the organ of Corti containing auditory receptor hair cells responsible for hearing. In contrast, the three semicircular canals and the otolith organ (consisting of the utriculus and sacculus) form the vestibular apparatus, which is responsible for maintaining body balance and posture.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The part of the internal ear responsible for hearing is the cochlea.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURALCONTROLANDCOORDINATION_MCQ_Q11 - Location of the organ of Corti

questiontext.text: The organ of corti is a structure present in

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The organ of Corti is the sensory apparatus of hearing that contains hair cells acting as auditory receptors.

Step 2: Evaluation
The organ of Corti is located on the basilar membrane within the scala media of the cochlea, which is part of the internal ear. The external ear (pinna and external auditory meatus) and middle ear (ear ossicles) transmit sound waves, while the semicircular canals are part of the vestibular apparatus for equilibrium.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The organ of Corti is a structure present in the cochlea.
